result.title: Beyond Prediction: Steering VLM Agents with Retrospective World Modeling
result.summary: Equipping VLM agents with world modeling capabilities has shown strong potential for complex reasoning and long-horizon planning, while reducing the dependence of policy learning on costly real-world interactions. Existing methods mainly rely on prospective simulation to predict the consequences of candidate actions. However, this forward-only paradigm focuses on what will happen next and provides limited constraints for verifying whether an action is causally consistent with the observed state transition, which can lead to plausible-looking but physically incoherent behaviors. In this paper, we challenge the view of world modeling as only prospective prediction and introduce Retrospective World Modeling, a new agent learning paradigm that enables agents to reason backward by estimating the retrospective attribution distribution $P(\hat{a}{t}|s_t, s{t+1})$ for the action that most likely caused a given transition. Based on this capability, we formulate the Self-Consistency Reward (SCR), an intrinsic signal that measures the probabilistic consistency between the policy action and the retrospective explanation. Integrating SCR into reinforcement learning provides dense transition-level feedback and steers agents toward behaviors that are both task-effective and physically grounded. Extensive experiments across diverse agentic tasks show that our method substantially improves policy robustness and generalization over prospective-only world modeling baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文重新审视「世界模型即前向预测」的观点，提出回溯式世界建模：从状态转移 (s_t, s_{t+1}) 反推最可能造成该转移的动作分布，并据此构造自一致性奖励（SCR）作为强化学习的稠密内在信号，在多种智能体任务上验证鲁棒性与泛化优于纯前瞻建模基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 的「使用与训练」主线相关：其由观测状态转移反推动作、并用一致性信号约束策略的做法，可供核查视觉证据筛选与推理状态训练监督中「状态是否真正被用于决策」这一因果贡献问题，但与 latent 推理状态生成的关系需读原文确认。
